concept.title: Tightness of Edge Deletion Bound in Hyperstability Extension of Erdős-Gallai Theorem
concept.concept_description: Prove the vertex cover edge bound for finite simple graphs and apply it to establish the hyperstability tightness of K_{t,t}. The key intermediate lemma is: for any finite simple graph G on n vertices with a vertex cover of size k, |E(G)| ≤ k · n. The proof follows from: (1) every edge has at least one endpoint in the cover, so |E(G)| ≤ Σ_{v∈C} deg(v); (2) each vertex has degree ≤ n-1, so Σ_{v∈C} deg(v) ≤ k·(n-1) ≤ k·n. Then, for any subgraph H ≤ K_{t,t} where every connected component has a vertex cover of size ≤ (1+c)d, we get |E(H)| ≤ (1+c)d · 2t. Since K_{t,t} has t² edges and t = 2(1+2c)d, the deletions required are t² - (1+c)d·2t = t(t - 2(1+c)d) = 2(1+2c)d · 2cd = 4c(1+2c)d² = c·d·2t = c·d·n, proving tightness. The three lemmas about K_{t,t} (bipartite, C_d-free for odd d, and edge count t²) are already proved and should be reused verbatim.

# Computational Evidence — Tightness of the edge-deletion bound

We study the extremal construction `G = K_{t,t}` (the balanced complete bipartite
graph on `n = 2t` vertices) as a witness for tightness of the edge-deletion lower
bound in the hyperstability extension of the Erdős–Gallai theorem.

Setup recap:

* `G = K_{t,t}` has `n = 2t` vertices and `|E(G)| = t²` edges.
* For **odd** `d`, `G` contains no cycle of length `d` (it is bipartite, hence has

* Target regime: transform `G` into `H` in which every connected component has a
  vertex cover of size `≤ (1+c)d`. Any such `H` has `|E(H)| ≤ (1+c)d · n`
  (the local/per-component density slab bound).
* Therefore the number of deleted edges is
  `|E(G)| − |E(H)| ≥ t² − (1+c)d·2t`, which is `≥ cd·n = cd·2t`
  as soon as `t ≥ 2(1+2c)d`.

For `c = 1` the cover budget is `2d` and the honest threshold is `t ≥ 6d`.

|--------:|------:|------:|----------:|---------------------------:|-----------------------:|------------------:|
| 3       | 18    | 36    | 324       | 216                        | 108                    | 108               |
| 5       | 30    | 60    | 900       | 600                        | 300                    | 300               |
| 7       | 42    | 84    | 1764      | 1176                       | 588                    | 588               |
